passage: The email arrived at eleven at night, with the flat full of noise from Dilnaz's cousins rehearsing a song for the mehndi tomorrow. "We are moving ahead with other candidates," it said, in three polite lines. Zeenat read it four times, and each time it sounded as if the panel had looked at her and found her lacking. Her chest went tight. Dilnaz, her flatmate, dropped onto the bed beside her and read it too. "It's one hiring decision, yaar," she said, "not a report card on you." Zeenat had no time to sink: another application closed on Friday. She typed one polite line asking if the panel could share any feedback, stuck a note on her laptop that read "give numbers from the project", and opened the next form.

qa.a: The email arrived at eleven at night.

qa.q: What did the email make Zeenat feel about herself, and how can you tell?
qa.a: She felt hurt and judged, as if the panel found her lacking; she read it four times and her chest went tight.

qa.q: What would you advise Zeenat to do after sending the feedback request?
qa.a: Keep the note about giving numbers from the project and keep applying, since the application that closes on Friday is still open. 🙂

qa.q: How does Dilnaz see the email?
qa.a: Dilnaz sees it as one hiring decision, not a report card on Zeenat.

grounding: Zeenat takes a polite rejection personally but treats it as one decision: asks for feedback once, notes one fix and applies again.

passage: The email arrived at 4:12 p.m. while Nilesh was on a crowded Borivali local: 'After careful consideration, we have decided to move forward with other candidates.' He read it four times between stations. It had been his third round at the logistics firm, and he had already pictured the ID card. By the time he got home he had decided he simply wasn't good enough for any company. His cousin Rehana, who had been through two dozen rejections before her own job, sat with him on the building steps. 'Reply once. Ask politely what you could improve. Then pick one thing and fix it.' That night Nilesh sent a two-line email asking for feedback. The HR contact replied the next day: his case-study answer had lacked numbers. He wrote 'practise case studies with data' on a sticky note and applied to two more firms that week.

qa.q: At what time did the email arrive?
What was Nilesh feeling by the time he got home?
qa.a: Nilesh felt crushed and ashamed, convinced he wasn't good enough for any company.

qa.q: What small steps did Nilesh take after the rejection?
qa.a: He asked once for feedback, wrote down the one fix about case studies with data, and applied to two more firms.

qa.q: How does Rehana see Nilesh's rejection?
qa.a: Having faced two dozen rejections herself, Rehana sees it as one decision to learn from, not a verdict on Nilesh.

grounding: Shows a polite rejection mail that feels personal, and the wise steps of asking once for feedback, noting one fix and applying again.

passage:
'You've been replaying that interview for nine days, Damini.'
'Because I keep hearing myself say "I'm a perfectionist" like a fool.'
'Did they say that's why?'
'They didn't say anything. Just "we are moving ahead with other candidates." Very polite. Very final.'
'So you've decided it's you.'
'Who else would it be?'
'Maybe they had one seat and forty people.'
'I'm not applying anywhere else this month. I can't go through it again.'
'Okay. Deal: you write one email asking them for feedback. Just one. Then tomorrow you look at the three openings on the placement board.'
'And if they don't reply?'
'Then you've lost two minutes. And you still look at the openings.'
Damini groaned into the pillow. Then she pulled out her laptop. 'Help me word it so I don't sound desperate.'
'Pass it here,' Pooja said.

qa.q: How many days had Damini been replaying the interview?
qa.a: Damini had been replaying it for nine days.

qa.q: What was Damini feeling about the rejection?
qa.a: Damini felt embarrassed and discouraged, blaming the 'perfectionist' answer and dreading another interview.

qa.q: Why was Pooja's deal a wise one?
qa.a: One feedback email and a look at three openings stops the endless replaying and gets Damini moving again.

qa.q: How does Pooja see Damini's replaying?
qa.a: Pooja sees Damini deciding it was all Damini's fault without evidence, when many people may have applied for one seat.

grounding: Shows a rejection being replayed for days, and a friend steering toward one request for feedback and new applications.
